newsitem.title: GERMANY: Dollar-sensitive stocks give German shares a boost.
newsitem.headline: Dollar-sensitive stocks give German shares a boost.

text.p: German shares, buoyed by the firmer dollar, were slightly higher in early bourse dealings on Tuesday as the German equities market found strength from dollar-sensitive shares.

The 30-share DAX index was up 13.67 points at 3,075.96 points in early dealings as the market remained positive ahead of Tuesday's U.S. Federal Reserve committee meeting at which the U.S. central bank was expected to keep rates steady.

Among the top blue-chip stocks underpinning the DAX due to the stronger dollar were industrial group Daimler-Benz AG, which gained 2.50 marks to 121.60 marks, and electronics group Siemens AG, which advanced 47 pfennigs to 83.30 marks.
Dealers said they expected the market to remain well supported if the dollar remained above 1.64 marks, the level at which it was trading in European dealings on Tuesday.

But traders were split between the perception that the share market, already trading around record levels, was due for a correction against hopes for an German economic upturn that would feed into corporate earnings.
"Fundamentally, there are still lots of things to be bullish about, but a correction of some kind has been overdue for some time now," one dealer said.
Another dealer, noting the patchy demand recorded on Monday despite strong gains, said that in the current bullish mood it was unclear where that correction might occur.
"It could be around 3,100, or it could be at 3,200," the dealer said.
Among other shares, chemicals group Degussa AG advanced two marks to 699 marks after reporting strong first-quarter results.

Metallgesellschaft AG was lower, falling 55 pfennigs to 33.25 marks, after some traders said the diversified industrial and engineering group's meeting with analysts to discuss its 1995/96 business year results was not received favourably.
